**Solution 1 (answer 3) is wrong.** It concludes that $H$ must be an induced subgraph of $P_4$, but $K_3$ is not. Subdivisions of $K_3$ are induced cycles of length at least 3, so a graph excludes all of them exactly when it has no cycles, i.e., it is a forest. Forests have bounded clique-width, so $K_3 \in \mathcal{P}$. Since $K_3 \not\subseteq_i P_4$, the set $\mathcal{M}$ must contain some larger graph, and $\mathcal{M} = \{P_4\}$ is impossible.

**Solution 2 (answer 6) is wrong.** Even granting its family $\mathcal{M} = \{C_3, P_4\}$, the problem asks for the sum of the *set* $\{|E(G)|\}$, which is $\{3\}$, giving 3, not 6. Its claim that $C_3$ is maximal is also unsupported, since the paw or $K_3+K_1$ could contain it.

**Solution 3 (answer 7) is not established.** It reaches 7 only through an unproven step that it openly flags. Its "pan" argument is also flawed: the paw is itself an induced subdivision of the paw, and it has only 4 vertices, so it contains no pan. The status of $K_3+K_1$ is left undecided, so the edge-count set is not determined. I could not verify the membership of the paw or $K_3+K_1$ in $\mathcal{P}$, so I cannot confirm 7 either.

None of the three solutions is supported by a complete argument, and two are refuted outright. I have not been able to confirm the true value of $\mathcal{M}$, so I cannot certify Solution 3's answer.

CHOICE: NONE
